standard_prerequisites.name: Set-quotient of an equivalence relation
standard_prerequisites.statement: For an equivalence relation (A,R) the quotient A/R is the set-quotient and c_R : A -> A/R is the quotient map.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the object on which the identity type is analysed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Mere propositions form a set
standard_prerequisites.statement: The universe of mere propositions is a set, by univalence.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what allows the double induction defining the extended relation at source lines 349-350.

standard_prerequisites.name: Encode-decode method
standard_prerequisites.statement: To identify a family with an identity type one defines a code family, a decoding map, and proves the two composites are identities.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the structure of the proof, and the author names it at source line 360.

core_obligations: Extend R to a relation R-tilde on A/R by double induction, using that the universe of propositions is a set, with the clauses R-tilde(c_R(x), c_R(y)) := R(x,y) and the equivalence induced by transitivity and symmetry (source lines 348-354).
Show R-tilde is reflexive by an easy induction, so that the direction (w = w') -> R-tilde(w,w') follows by transport (source line 357).
For the converse direction note that R-tilde(w,w') -> (w = w') is a mere proposition, so by surjectivity of c_R it suffices to treat w, w' of the form c_R(x), c_R(y) (source line 358).
In that case produce the canonical map R(x,y) -> (c_R(x) = c_R(y)), which completes the encode-decode comparison and hence the equivalence (source line 359).

proof_roadmap.step: Define the extended relation on the quotient by double induction.
One direction by transport from reflexivity; the other reduced to representatives of the quotient.
Supply the canonical map and read off the equivalence.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.1.8 at source lines 339-345: for an equivalence relation (A,R) the identification type c_R(x) = c_R(y) is equivalent to R(x,y), i.e. equivalence relations are effective. The author's proof (source lines 347-361) is a full encode-decode argument rather than a citation: the relation is first extended to the quotient by double induction, which is legitimate only because the universe of propositions is a set (lines 348-354), the direction from identities to the relation is then obtained by transport after proving reflexivity (line 357), and the converse can be reduced to representatives of the quotient because the goal is a mere proposition and the quotient map is surjective (line 358), with the canonical map completing the comparison (line 359). The author notes at the end that this is the encode-decode method, which the statement does not reveal.
